taxonomyNote: NatureServe and ADW place it in Polychrotidae; NatureServe notes a revised anole taxonomy (Poe et al. 2017) followed by Nicholson (2025) that treats anoles differently.
fieldMarks: Slender lizard 4-8 cm (body) with a tail over half the total length; 2-6 g.
Colour changes between green, brown and grey with temperature and excitement; dark brown or black typically signals cold or stress.
Males usually have a pinkish dewlap under the throat that is extended in displays, rarely seen in females; females often have a pale dorsal line from neck to tail base.
behavior: Diurnal, sitting on a perch and watching for prey; usually stays within a small territory (about 50-100 m2) and bobs its head in displays.
Eats insects, spiders and other small arthropods; does not hibernate and can be active on sunny winter days.
Mostly arboreal; climbs trunks, shrubs, fence posts and building walls and sleeps in vegetation at night.
habitat: Wide range of edge habitats: upland forest, pine-palmetto scrub, rocky escarpments, swamps, wooded parks, fields, maritime scrub and residential lots.
range: NatureServe lists it in the southeastern US (North Carolina to Florida, west to Oklahoma and Texas, north to Tennessee and Arkansas); Hawaii is listed as introduced.
